definitions.explanation: Describes a situation or a person's movements as rushed and without pause. Unlike {忙|いそが}しい, which simply reports having a lot to do, {忙|せわ}しい conveys the unsettled, hurried feel of it.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{忙|せわ}しい。
examples.english: The end of the year is hectic.

examples.japanese: {忙|せわ}しく{動|うご}き{回|まわ}る{店員|てんいん}を{見|み}ていた。
examples.english: I was watching the shop staff bustling about.

examples.japanese: {都会|とかい}の{忙|せわ}しい{暮|く}らしに{疲|つか}れて、{田舎|いなか}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}すことにした。
examples.english: Worn out by the restless pace of city life, I decided to move to the countryside.

notes:
Written with the same kanji as {忙|いそが}しい but read せわしい; the reading is usually clear from context, and writers often use kana to avoid ambiguity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {忙|せわ}しく{働|はたら}く: to work at a hurried pace
- {忙|せわ}しい{毎日|まいにち}: hectic days
- {気|き}ぜわしい: fidgety, on edge (a related compound)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忙|せわ}しない: restless, fidgety — the more common form in speech; nearly the same meaning despite the ない ending
- {忙|いそが}しい: busy — neutral report of having much to do, without the restless nuance
